calls.title: DEEPA MENON and Chris Sanders + Cary Rakin
calls.summary: The team discussed the technical and commercial implications of using multi-org versus multiple instances for InMobi's platforms, including Exchange, DSP, and Glance. Key points included the structure of license keys, where multi-org setups share a license but separate instances require individual keys, thus increasing costs. Urgency was emphasized to finalize licensing options for these platforms, with considerations for three initial licenses if separate instances are selected. There were also discussions regarding SSO configurations, which are global per instance and complicate the multi-org setup with shared email domains. Recommendations leaned toward using teams within a single org for better data segregation. Next steps included addressing gaps in documentation and securing a new license for the DSP team while awaiting further clarifications.
calls.keywords: multi-org, license key, self-hosted, SSO configuration, GrowthBook, instance

calls.title: DEEPA MENON and Chris Sanders + Cary Rakin
calls.summary: The team discussed multi-org setup technicalities and licensing implications essential for aligning with InMobi's complex organization and legal requirements. Deepa Menon highlighted the need for cost understanding related to separate license keys for different legal entities, while Cary Rakin confirmed that distinct setups require separate contracts, with potential cost savings for multi-tenant configurations. The urgency of acquiring at least three license keys for different initial instances was emphasized. Technical constraints regarding role-based access and SSO configurations were addressed, particularly how identical email domains impact multi-org setups. Proposed solutions included using teams within a single org for data separation, and immediate licensing was approved for the DSP operations to avoid delays.
